clue.text: Personal history recorded with application

parts.note: a written record of one's career that a job seeker sends along with an application form

explanation.definitionFit: A résumé is the written personal history of education and career that accompanies a job application.

clue.text: Cane? One's no good for supplying the teachers!

parts.note: a staff is a stick or cane
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark that corporal punishment is a poor way to find teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cane used in schools, but it is just the stick, a staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffing a school means providing it with its teachers and other employees.

clue.text: Bavarian part song

indicators.note: part says the answer is only a portion of the word Bavarian

explanation.surface: A partsong from Bavaria, sung in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Rev Dunne's upset, disconcerted …

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A clergyman called Dunne is rattled and flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnerved and disconcerted are synonyms, both meaning thrown off balance or made uneasy.

clue.text: … a man of the cloth

parts.note: usually a clergyman, as the previous clue's Rev suggests, but read literally a man whose trade is fabric

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 4 down, so the reader expects another clergyman; a mercer is a dealer in textiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercer is a trader in fine cloth such as silk, literally a man dealing in cloth.

clue.text: Glass vessel

definitions.meaning: a tall drinking glass, used especially for sherry or beer
a sailing ship with two or more masts rigged fore and aft

explanation.surface: A container made of glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a large sherry or beer glass and a fore-and-aft rigged sailing ship.

clue.text: A display of rubbish in addition

parts.note: tat is cheap, worthless goods: rubbish
too means also, in addition

explanation.surface: An exhibition that is also an exhibition of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: A tattoo here is a military display of marching and music, such as the Edinburgh Tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an evening military display or pageant with bands and drill.

clue.text: Mostly modern TA trained to the highest degree and ready for battle

indicators.note: trained means drilled into shape, so these letters are rearranged
mostly says the word modern loses its last letter

parts.note: the word taken as it is before trimming
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
in the idiom 'to the teeth', the teeth stand for the utmost extent, the highest degree

explanation.surface: Today's Territorial Army, thoroughly drilled and fully prepared for combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the N of MODERN; 'trained' shuffles MODER and TA into ARMED TO. The clue's 'to' joins this to the idiom 'to the teeth', meaning to the highest degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fully equipped with weapons is prepared for battle; the idiom stresses complete arming.

clue.text: Out-and-out expert takes in number, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: out-and-out means complete or utter

indicators.note: takes in means the expert word holds the number inside it

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A thorough specialist absorbing figures, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterance means the way a person speaks, their style of expression or delivery.

clue.text: Conduct church broadcast

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Running a church service that goes out on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to conduct or preside over it.

clue.text: Take financial action when game official's delayed

parts.note: a ref is a referee, the official in a game; 's is read as is
late means delayed

explanation.surface: Economic policy is set in motion when the referee arrives late.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflate an economy is to boost spending and credit, a deliberate financial measure.

clue.text: Sign of mirth when clothier loses one after tailoring

indicators.note: tailoring means cutting and reshaping, so the remaining letters are rearranged
loses says a letter is dropped from the word clothier

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tailor's chuckle once a garment is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes I (one) out of CLOTHIER, leaving CLOTHER, which 'after tailoring' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, an audible sign of amusement.

clue.text: Firm in the money

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A business that is doing well financially.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin is a piece of metal money, and coin also means money in general.

clue.text: Cricket commentator's words signifying end of transmission

definitions.meaning: a commentator might say a set of six balls is complete and a batsman dismissed in one breath
the radio operator's sign-off closing a message

explanation.surface: A cricket broadcaster signs off at the end of the programme.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, and out means a batsman is dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the radio sign-off ending a message and also two cricket calls.

clue.text: One behind, pull goal back after losing ball

indicators.note: back says the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: drag means pull

indicators.note: losing says a letter is taken out of the word goal

parts.note: the word taken as it is before trimming
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A team trailing by one tries to pull a goal back but loses the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One behind' and 'pull goal back' paint a football match, but 'back' turns the whole run, and 'after losing' drops O from the goal word first.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is someone who falls behind or lags behind others.

clue.text: Honour account company's to deal out

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company; 's is a link

indicators.note: out here means disordered, so the word deal is rearranged

explanation.surface: An award for a business that hands out its accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an honour or award granted in recognition of merit.

clue.text: The significance of mainly unadulterated wine

indicators.note: mainly says most of the word is kept and the last letter goes

parts.note: pure means unadulterated
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Asking what pure, unmixed wine signifies.
explanation.definitionFit: The purport of something is its meaning or general significance.

clue.text: Crest Hotel in unusual place

indicators.note: in says the hotel word sits inside the other letters
unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters of place are rearranged

parts.note: an inn is a hotel

explanation.surface: A Crest Hotel found in an odd location.
explanation.walkthrough: Crest Hotels was a British hotel chain, so the surface reads as a hotel name; 'Crest' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a peak or summit, the crest of a mountain.

clue.text: I'm not taking part, I see

definitions.text: I'm not taking part, I see

parts.words: I'm not taking part, I see
parts.note: the words of someone who watches rather than participates

explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker is a spectator who watches an event without joining in.

clue.text: Doctor meant to change the remedy

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

indicators.note: to change says the letters of meant are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor intended to switch the treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicament is a medicine or substance used to treat illness, a remedy.

clue.text: Dismal record and one goes for religious education

indicators.note: goes for says one letter is replaced by another piece

parts.note: a diary is a record of events
one is the Roman numeral I
RE is religious education, a British school subject

explanation.surface: A gloomy logbook where a child swaps one lesson for scripture class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes for' puts RE in place of the I in DIARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary and dismal are synonyms meaning gloomy and depressing.

clue.text: Sign of distress in time of celebration

definitions.meaning: the first of May, a spring festival and workers' holiday

explanation.surface: A call for help in the middle of a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the spoken emergency signal and May Day, a traditional festival day.

clue.text: Reportedly, the long jumper is to make a dash for it

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a flea is famous for jumping great distances relative to its size

explanation.surface: An athlete in the long jump is said to be running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the long jumper' suggests an athlete, but it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away quickly, to make a dash for it.

clue.text: Left English daily to sustain circulation in theory

indicators.note: circulation means moving round, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An English newspaper on the left hoping to keep its readership up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulation' suggests a newspaper's sales but signals the rearrangement of L, E and DAILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in an ideal world, as things should be in principle: in theory.

clue.text: Unaccompanied sailor has seafood

parts.note: AB is able seaman, a sailor
alone means unaccompanied

explanation.surface: A solitary seaman tucks into some shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail prized as a delicacy, a type of seafood.

clue.text: Book functions

definitions.meaning: the ... of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament
performs or functions as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Acts is a book of the Bible, and to act is to function or operate.

clue.text: Description of smoke I had after current resistance?

indicators.note: after puts the I-had piece behind the two electrical pieces

parts.note: AC is alternating current
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: An electrician's question about smoke after current met resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp and bitter to smell or taste, a typical description of smoke.

clue.text: It's not usually part of one's homeland

definitions.text: It's not usually part of one's homeland

parts.words: It's not usually part of one's homeland
parts.note: a plot of ground for growing vegetables, usually away from the house and its garden

explanation.walkthrough: 'homeland' suggests a country; read literally it is land at one's home. A British allotment is a rented vegetable plot, usually away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a rented plot of land, usually away from one's own home and garden.
